authorship: Independently authored explanations of this picker. Original-picker wording was consulted to identify intended scope, not copied or closely paraphrased.
credit: RuneScape Wiki contributors; game facts are supported by per-entry pinned revisions. Engine effects were checked against the authored core and selected private task records.
licence: Wiki-derived facts and adaptations: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. Independently authored interface explanations remain separate from original-picker text.

Skillcape.what: Adds listed skillcape and milestone-cape goals when their sellers, materials and skill requirements are reachable. These can become the highest goal shown for a skill.
Skillcape.example: With Hickton reachable and Fletching training available, buying a Fletching cape can become a goal at 99 Fletching.
Skillcape.grindWarning: A cape goal can turn a local task list into a level-99 training commitment.

Rare Drop.what: Allows item sources at every recorded drop rate. Turning it off removes sources that fail your rare-drop cutoff; another eligible source can keep the item available.
Rare Drop.example: An “obtain a goblin champion’s scroll” goal can appear with this on; a restrictive cutoff can remove it when no other eligible source exists.
Rare Drop.grindWarning: Including very rare sources can create long, chance-based collection or equipment grinds.

Pouch.what: This saved switch currently has no task-generation effect. Runecrafting pouch access and requirements do not change when you toggle it.
Pouch.example: No task is added here: switching this on does not create a goal to obtain a medium Runecrafting pouch.

InsidePOH.what: Allows house furniture-workbench tasks above level 1 and the items they produce. Level-1 tasks stay available; the separate workbench-training switch decides whether these methods can justify further Construction training.
InsidePOH.example: Turning this off removes the eligible clay-fireplace construction task at the furniture workbench, because it is above level 1.

InsidePOH Primary.what: Lets house furniture-workbench methods count as repeatable Construction training. Turning it off can reduce the levels the picker thinks you can train to, while leaving furniture recipes available.
InsidePOH Primary.example: Constructing a clay fireplace can establish Construction training with this on; with it off, that recipe no longer supplies a primary training route.

Construction Milestone.what: Adds the listed Construction milestones, such as changing a house style or building certain rooms. Their own location, quest and level requirements still apply.
Construction Milestone.example: If the estate agent and requirements are reachable, changing your house to the basic stone style can become a goal.

Boss.what: Lets loot from monsters on the picker’s boss list supply items and collections. It does not independently require boss kills or enable boss kill-count goals.
Boss.example: If the King Black Dragon is reachable, its Dragon Rider gloves can become an item source with this on.
Boss.grindWarning: Boss loot can lead to repeated kills; access alone does not establish that you can win the fight.

Slayer Equipment.what: Adds listed goals to equip specialist Slayer gear. A goal still needs a source for the item and the required Slayer and combat levels.
Slayer Equipment.example: Wielding a mirror shield can become a goal when the item, 25 Slayer and 20 Defence are within reach.

Normal Farming.what: Lets listed ordinary Farming methods establish repeatable Farming training. Turning this off does not by itself remove every crop recipe or Farming product.
Normal Farming.example: Growing potatoes can establish a Farming training route with this on; disabling it removes that route’s primary-training status.

Raking.what: Allows the recorded patch-raking method to supply weeds and establish Farming training when a suitable patch is reachable.
Raking.example: Raking weeds from an accessible farming patch can become a Farming method; turning this off blocks that method.

Kill X.what: Adds a kill-count goal for each eligible reachable monster, using your chosen count. Boss, Slayer, Skiller and backlog restrictions still apply, and completion needs your checkmark.
Kill X.example: With chickens reachable and the amount set to 25, a “Kill 25 chickens” goal can appear.
Kill X.grindWarning: A large count applies to every eligible monster, so small settings changes can add many kills.

Kill X Boss.what: Includes monsters on the picker’s boss list in kill-count goals when Kill X is enabled. Their access and Slayer requirements still apply.
Kill X Boss.example: With Kill X on and the King Black Dragon reachable, this can add a kill-count goal for that boss.
Kill X Boss.grindWarning: Your configured count also applies to bosses, which can make the requirement much longer.

Sorceress's Garden.what: Allows the listed herb-or-fruit picking method in Sorceress’s Garden to establish Farming training. Garden access still has to be available.
Sorceress's Garden.example: Picking herbs or sq’irk fruit in Sorceress’s Garden can count as a Farming method when this is on.

Spells.what: Allows listed spellcasting tasks and their products, including spells used by other skills. Runes, spell unlocks and training requirements still apply.
Spells.example: Casting Water Strike can become a Magic goal when its rune and equipment requirements are reachable.

Show Skill Tasks.what: Shows active skill goals when skill tasks are enabled. Hiding them leaves the underlying recipes, sources and reachable-training calculations in place.
Show Skill Tasks.example: Turning this off removes a displayed oak-chopping goal from the active task list.

Show Quest Tasks.what: Shows active quest steps and whole-quest goals when quests are enabled. Hiding them does not remove quest prerequisites from other tasks.
Show Quest Tasks.example: Turning this off hides an available Cook’s Assistant completion goal. Basic quest requirements still apply elsewhere.

Show Diary Tasks.what: Enables the listed area-achievement tasks and their rewards. The separate Achievement switch controls whether eligible achievements appear in the active list.
Show Diary Tasks.example: Turning this off can remove the Easy Lumbridge tier and its achievement-reward route from eligibility.

Show Best in Slot Tasks.what: Shows goals to obtain the picker’s highest-ranked reachable combat equipment. Comparisons use recorded stats, compatible loadouts and equipment requirements.
Show Best in Slot Tasks.example: An obtainable bronze full helm can become an armour goal when it wins the comparison among your reachable helmets.

Show Best in Slot Prayer Tasks.what: Adds equipment comparisons by Prayer bonus alongside combat-style comparisons. The main equipment-goal and Prayer-equipment rules must also be enabled.
Show Best in Slot Prayer Tasks.example: An obtainable priest gown top can become a Prayer equipment goal when its Prayer bonus wins that slot.

Show Best in Slot Defensive Tasks.what: Adds defensive equipment goals. Ordinary slots rank armour first and life points second; compatible hand combinations rank their total armour plus life points.
Show Best in Slot Defensive Tasks.example: A reachable bronze kiteshield can become part of the selected defensive hand setup when it wins that comparison.

Show Best in Slot Melee Style Tasks.what: Compares melee weapons separately for stab, slash and crush instead of selecting only an overall melee winner. Compatible hand and ammunition rules still apply.
Show Best in Slot Melee Style Tasks.example: A bronze scimitar can become the slash weapon goal when it wins the reachable slash comparison.

Show Best in Slot 1H and 2H.what: Keeps the best two-handed setup and the best alternative hand setup as separate equipment goals. It can therefore require more than the single overall winning weapon setup.
Show Best in Slot 1H and 2H.example: If the bronze 2h sword wins overall, this can retain an obtainable bronze scimitar setup as the other hand-mode goal.

Show Best in Slot Shield.what: Keeps a winning shield setup alongside the other selected weapon setups. It applies to compatible combat, Prayer and defensive comparisons.
Show Best in Slot Shield.example: An obtainable bronze kiteshield can remain an equipment goal even when a two-handed setup scores better overall.

Consumable Primary BiS.what: Requires consumable equipment, such as arrows, to have a supply that meets your required-training rules before it can win an equipment comparison. Other supplies can leave an item obtainable without making it a required equipment goal.
Consumable Primary BiS.example: A bronze-arrow equipment goal can disappear if its only reachable source fails your primary-supply cutoff.

Non-permanent BiS.what: Includes equipment that expires or crumbles after use in recommended gear and wielding goals. Turning it off keeps repairable or rechargeable items and ammunition eligible.
Non-permanent BiS.example: Turning this off excludes a corrupt dragon scimitar from equipment goals because it crumbles to dust.
Non-permanent BiS.grindWarning: An expiring winner may need repeated replacements; the picker’s score does not subtract that upkeep.

Show Quest Tasks Complete.what: Shows whole-quest completion goals instead of individual quest-step goals. A whole quest still needs every required step, item and location to be reachable.
Show Quest Tasks Complete.example: For Cook’s Assistant, this hides individual preparation steps and keeps the whole-quest completion goal when eligible.

Show Diary Tasks Complete.what: Restricts active achievement goals to recorded whole-tier completion markers. Individual duties can still carry prerequisites and reward evidence behind the active list.
Show Diary Tasks Complete.example: An eligible Easy Lumbridge tier remains a goal, while its separate individual duties are hidden.

Show Diary Tasks Any.what: Lets individual area achievements appear even while an earlier tier remains blocked. Each duty still needs its own requirements; an available tier goal can group several duties.
Show Diary Tasks Any.example: “Are Yew As Fired Up As I Am?” can appear while an earlier Lumbridge tier is blocked, if you can burn the required yew log at the gatehouse.

Highest Level.what: Allows higher recipes to compete for a consumable ingredient instead of initially limiting it to its lowest eligible recipe. The active skill view still selects its highest available goal; some special task links remain unsupported.
Highest Level.example: Crafting an unfired bowl can become the soft-clay processing goal instead of stopping at an unfired pot, when the higher recipe and training are eligible.

BIS Skilling.what: Shows listed skilling tools and convenience upgrades. Explicit equipment sets use the priorities recorded in the data; the picker does not invent a universal ranking for unrelated tools.
BIS Skilling.example: Obtaining the dwarven army axe can appear as a skilling-equipment goal when its source is reachable.

BIS Skilling Consumables.what: Includes the listed expendable skilling supplies among skilling-equipment goals. Their source, level and equipment-set requirements still apply.
BIS Skilling Consumables.example: Obtaining a crystal skillchompa can become a skilling-supply goal when the recorded requirements are met.
BIS Skilling Consumables.grindWarning: These supplies are consumed in use; obtaining one does not prove a lasting stock.

BIS Skilling Relics.what: Allows listed skilling relic unlock goals and their recorded prerequisites. The picker does not choose a simultaneous relic setup or allocate monolith energy, and some interactions with skilling goals remain incomplete.
BIS Skilling Relics.example: Unlocking Pouch Protector can appear when its required relic item is obtainable.

Collection Log.what: Enables the declared collection-log item goals. The matching boss, Slayer, skilling or breeding subrule and each goal’s own requirements still apply.
Collection Log.example: With the Slayer log subrule enabled, obtaining goblin mail can become a collection goal.
Collection Log.grindWarning: Completing a log can require repeated drops long after useful equipment has been obtained.

Boss Collection Log.what: Includes declared boss-log items when Collection Log is enabled. Item access still follows boss-source and drop-rate rules.
Boss Collection Log.example: Obtaining Dragon Rider gloves can become a King Black Dragon log goal when the gloves are obtainable.
Boss Collection Log.grindWarning: A boss-log item is a chance-based target, so a fixed number of kills is not guaranteed to finish it.

Slayer Collection Log.what: Includes declared Slayer-log items when Collection Log is enabled. These are item collection goals, not instructions to obtain a Slayer assignment.
Slayer Collection Log.example: An obtainable goblin mail can become an Asgarnia and Misthalin Slayer-log goal.

Skilling Collection Log.what: Includes the declared skilling-log goals when Collection Log is enabled. The task data supplies the item requirements and log grouping.
Skilling Collection Log.example: An obtainable warped stone can become a Dungeoneering collection goal.

Archaeology Collections.what: Adds goals to complete the listed Archaeology collections. The named collector and every required restored artefact must be reachable.
Archaeology Collections.example: Completing Art Critic Jacques’s Anarchic Abstraction collection can become a goal once its artefacts and collector are available.

Universal Tertiary.what: Allows the recorded universal-tertiary prerequisite to unlock certain special item sources. It changes source eligibility rather than adding a visible goal to collect every tertiary drop.
Universal Tertiary.example: Turning this off can remove an “obtain a mimic kill token” goal by blocking its recorded tertiary source, even with unique-item goals enabled.

Breeding Log.what: Allows the listed animal-breeding collection goals and breeding-log achievement requirements. Other rules and each animal’s recorded access requirements still apply.
Breeding Log.example: Breeding a common brown rabbit at Manor Farm can become a collection goal when the matching log rules and requirements are enabled.
Breeding Log.grindWarning: Completing breeding goals can require repeated breeding attempts for missing varieties.

Minigame.what: Allows listed minigame tasks and shops to supply methods and items. Turning it off blocks those recorded routes rather than every activity commonly called a minigame.
Minigame.example: A Temple Trekking Agility-tome method can become a training route when this is on and its prerequisites are reachable.

Shortcut Task.what: Shows listed shortcut goals above level 1 in the active skill list. The separate shortcut-training switch decides whether crossing them can justify further Agility training.
Shortcut Task.example: Turning this off hides the “cross the crumbling wall in Falador” skill goal; that shortcut remains in the underlying activity catalogue.

Shortcut.what: Lets listed shortcuts establish repeatable Agility training. The separate shortcut-display rule controls whether their skill goals appear.
Shortcut.example: Crossing an accessible stile can count as an Agility method with this on; turning it off removes that method’s primary-training status.

Wield Crafted Items.what: Lets crafted equipment supply eligible combat training, equipment comparisons and listed skilling-equipment requirements. Without it, a processing recipe alone does not prove a usable equipment source.
Wield Crafted Items.example: Smithing a bronze sword can supply the equipment for a wielding or combat-training goal with this on.

Wield Crafted Items Override.what: This compatibility switch has no exact implementation here. It does not override the crafted-equipment restriction or add equipment tasks.
Wield Crafted Items Override.example: No task is added here: a crafted bronze sword still follows Wield Crafted Items when this override is toggled.

Multi Step Processing.what: Allows eligible recipes to use products of earlier processing steps. Conditional multi-step products do not automatically prove equipment access or Extra collection goals.
Multi Step Processing.example: A leather body recipe can use leather made by an earlier tanning step when the processing and training conditions allow it.

Puro-Puro.what: Lets the picker open the listed Puro-Puro area automatically when you have a valid way in. Turning this off shuts off that area and the impling methods within it.
Puro-Puro.example: Catching a baby impling in Puro-Puro can become a Hunter goal with this on and the area reachable.

Extra implings.what: Allows the listed impling catches at additional fixed locations. This is separate from opening Puro-Puro and from wandering-impling rules.
Extra implings.example: Catching a young impling in the Al Kharid resource dungeon can become a Hunter goal when that dungeon is reachable.

Bakami.what: This switch cannot currently activate the recorded bakami catches: those records use an unsupported requirement field. They remain unavailable when the rule is enabled.
Bakami.example: No task is added here: catching an oily bakami remains unsupported even though this is a real Arc creature.

Farming Primary.what: Lets ingredients grown through Farming support required skill training. Turning it off leaves those ingredients obtainable, but they no longer justify required training by themselves.
Farming Primary.example: If your only white berries come from growing a whiteberry bush, this can let them support a super defence training goal.

Secondary Primary.what: Lets methods marked as secondary, such as small reward hand-ins, count as a way to train a skill for required goals. Their ingredients must still come from supplies that meet your training rules.
Secondary Primary.example: A listed Agility City Quest hand-in can establish Agility training with this on and the required hand-in item available.

Secondary Primary Amount.what: Sets how common an ingredient drop must be before it can justify required training or consumable equipment goals. Enter a denominator or probability; zero accepts all known rates, and the inclusive switch decides whether equality passes.
Secondary Primary Amount.example: With a 1/16 cutoff, a super defence training goal needs its dropped white berries to pass that probability test; equality follows the inclusive switch.

RDT.what: Allows the recorded rare, gem and Wilderness drop-table branches to supply items. Turning it off removes those branches while leaving ordinary monster loot intact.
RDT.example: If a dragon helm is your winning helmet and is obtainable only through the rare drop table, switching this off removes its obtain goal.

Crystal chests.what: Allows the listed crystal-chest opening methods and their loot to supply items. The correct chest, key and access requirements must be reachable.
Crystal chests.example: Opening the Taverley crystal chest with a crystal key can supply an uncut dragonstone with this on.

Untracked Uniques.what: Enables the declared unique-item goals outside the main collection-log groups. A matching subcategory switch and each item’s requirements still apply.
Untracked Uniques.example: With its skilling subrule on, obtaining golden leaping trout eggs can become a collection goal.
Untracked Uniques.grindWarning: Some unique items are rare rewards; this can add substantial collection work without improving equipment.

Untracked Uniques Skilling.what: Includes the listed unique skilling items when Untracked Uniques is enabled. These goals use the sources recorded for each item.
Untracked Uniques Skilling.example: Obtaining golden leaping trout eggs for an aquarium can become a collection goal.

Untracked Uniques Combat.what: Includes the listed combat uniques when Untracked Uniques is enabled. Drop-rate and source rules still decide which items are obtainable.
Untracked Uniques Combat.example: Obtaining a goblin champion’s scroll can become a combat-unique goal when an eligible drop source is reachable.
Untracked Uniques Combat.grindWarning: Champion scrolls can take many thousands of kills; this goal has no guaranteed kill limit.

Untracked Uniques Minigames.what: Includes the declared minigame uniques when Untracked Uniques is enabled. Recorded minigame access, shops and reward prerequisites still apply.
Untracked Uniques Minigames.example: Obtaining the gold dwarf multicannon upgrade can become a collection goal when the Artisans’ Workshop reward is available.

Ceremonial Swords.what: Adds the listed individual ceremonial sword and off-hand sword collection goals. Their recorded items and membership requirements still apply.
Ceremonial Swords.example: Obtaining iron ceremonial sword I can become a goal when the ceremonial sword route is reachable.
Ceremonial Swords.grindWarning: Keeping a ceremonial sword requires a perfect result from its randomly offered design.

Untracked Uniques Daemonheim.what: Includes the declared Daemonheim uniques when Untracked Uniques is enabled. These are collection objectives, not proof that a reward can be carried outside a dungeon.
Untracked Uniques Daemonheim.example: Obtaining a celestial surgebox inside Daemonheim can become a unique-item goal.

Untracked Uniques Misc.what: Includes miscellaneous declared uniques when Untracked Uniques is enabled. This covers the recorded goals that do not belong to the other unique-item groups.
Untracked Uniques Misc.example: Obtaining fancy boots from the Stronghold of Security can become a collection goal.

Ports Scrolls.what: Adds listed Player-Owned Ports scroll goals and permits related achievement requirements. Scroll goals depend on the recorded port access and other rules.
Ports Scrolls.example: Obtaining the reefwalker’s cape scroll can become a goal when Player-Owned Ports is reachable.
Ports Scrolls.grindWarning: The complete cape scroll needs four pieces, so one successful scroll voyage does not finish the unlock.

Slayer Souls.what: Allows the listed soul-capture goals. They use the recorded ushabti and monster requirements; the picker cannot verify that an in-game capture succeeded.
Slayer Souls.example: Collecting a goblin soul can become a goal when an empty ushabti and a qualifying goblin are reachable.
Slayer Souls.grindWarning: Soul capture is chance-based, so obtaining the container does not complete the soul collection.

Dungeoneering Journals.what: This saved switch currently has no matching generated journal goals or engine consumer. Toggling it does not add a journal-collection requirement.
Dungeoneering Journals.example: No task is added here: collecting a Daemonheim journal page remains outside this rule’s task generation.

Combat and Teleport Spells.what: Allows the listed combat and teleport spell goals when Spells is enabled. It does not itself grant a destination, spell unlock or rune supply.
Combat and Teleport Spells.example: Casting Water Strike can appear as a Magic goal with both spell switches enabled and its requirements reachable.

Primary Spawns.what: Treats ground-item spawns as a reliable enough ingredient supply to require skill training. It also lets spawned consumable gear compete in equipment goals; turning this off leaves the items obtainable.
Primary Spawns.example: If white berries north of the Tirannwn lodestone are your only berry source, turning this off can remove the super defence training goal.

Smithing by Smelting.what: Lets Smithing processing establish training without a reachable anvil. Ore, furnace and recipe requirements still apply.
Smithing by Smelting.example: Smelting bronze bars can support a Smithing goal even when you have a furnace but no reachable anvil.

Pets.what: Allows listed pet-related goals. Other rules, sources and the pet’s skill requirements still decide which goals appear.
Pets.example: Obtaining a sneakerpeeper pet can become a goal when its reward source and required skills are reachable.
Pets.grindWarning: Optional pet goals can add substantial training or chance-based work beyond ordinary equipment upgrades.

Kill X Amount.what: Sets the positive whole-number count shown in Kill X goals. Changing it updates the target count without creating a new task identity or recording kills for you.
Kill X Amount.example: Changing the amount from 1 to 25 turns an existing chicken goal into “Kill 25 chickens”.

Rare Drop Amount.what: Sets the probability cutoff used when Rare Drop is off. A denominator means 1 divided by that number; zero accepts all rates, and Rare Drop Inclusive decides whether equality passes.
Rare Drop Amount.example: A restrictive cutoff can remove the “obtain a goblin champion’s scroll” goal by excluding its only eligible drop source.

Manually Complete Tasks.what: This saved switch currently has no task-generation effect. It does not switch completion into a separate manual mode or mark goals complete.
Manually Complete Tasks.example: No task is added here: an available Cook’s Assistant goal still uses the normal completion controls when this is toggled.

Every Drop.what: Adds item-collection goals from eligible monsters and listed loot-producing activities. You can choose an alternative source for the same item; source access and rare-drop filters still apply.
Every Drop.example: With chickens reachable, collecting a feather can become an item goal. Another eligible feather source can be an alternative.
Every Drop.grindWarning: Collecting every eligible item can add rare-drop grinds; a checkmark does not prove you still own the item.

HigherLander.what: This saved switch currently has no engine or presentation effect. Toggling it does not alter task levels, sources or active goals.
HigherLander.example: No task is added or removed here: a bronze-sword wielding goal follows the normal equipment and training rules.

Secondary MTA.what: This compatibility switch has no exact Mage Training Arena implementation here. It does not relax the arena task’s rune-source requirements.
Secondary MTA.example: No task is added here: participating in Mage Training Arena still needs the normally eligible rune supplies.

Skilling Pets.what: Includes declared skilling-pet collection goals when Pets is enabled. It does not guarantee a pet drop or prove that your training method can award one.
Skilling Pets.example: Obtaining Dojo Mojo can become an Agility-pet goal when its recorded source is eligible.
Skilling Pets.grindWarning: A pet roll is random; reaching the displayed skill goal does not guarantee the pet.

Permanent Unlockables.what: Adds goals for one-time upgrades that stay unlocked, such as building a rope rack or applying Innate Mastery to a weapon. Turning it off does not remove the separate rope-rack Construction goals.
Permanent Unlockables.example: Building the Eagles’ Peak rope rack can become an unlock goal when its location and materials are reachable; the parallel Construction task is separate.
Permanent Unlockables.grindWarning: Innate Mastery uses a Shard of Genesis Essence, a hard-mode boss reward; these goals can take much longer than building a rope rack.

Prayers.what: Allows the specifically listed prayer-use goal when its requirements are reachable. This does not generate a goal for every prayer or replace the separate prayer-unlock rules.
Prayers.example: Using Smite can become a Prayer goal when its level requirement is reachable.

All Droptables.what: Adds collection goals for the recorded item quantities in eligible monster and activity loot tables. Quantity ranges remain ranges; missing or cyclic tables do not create goals.
All Droptables.example: A recorded chicken feather drop can create a feather-quantity goal rather than only an “obtain a feather” goal.
All Droptables.grindWarning: Different quantities can create multiple goals for one item, increasing the collection workload.

All Droptables Nest.what: Would add quantity goals for obtainable nests that have both a loot table and a matching nest-loot task. The current retained data has no matching nest-loot task, so this adds no nest goals.
All Droptables Nest.example: No task is added here: a bird’s nest seed-loot collection goal cannot be generated from the current task data.

Every Drop Implings.what: Includes listed eligible impling loot sources when Every Drop is enabled. Catch access, item-source rules and drop-rate filters still apply.
Every Drop Implings.example: A reachable baby impling catch can contribute its eligible loot items to Every Drop goals.

Skiller.what: Excludes monster-drop item sources, kill-count goals and tasks marked unsuitable for skillers. This is partial support; it does not implement every restriction of a combat-free account.
Skiller.example: Turning this on removes chicken kill-count goals and chicken-drop sources such as feathers.

Fill Stash.what: Adds the listed hidey-hole filling goals. Each goal needs its location, construction prerequisite and complete set of emote-clue items to be reachable.
Fill Stash.example: Filling the Lumbridge Swamp shed hidey-hole can become a goal once its required equipment and build task are available.

All Shops.what: Adds buy-each-item goals for specific reachable shops and listed shop activities. A completed collection goal does not record current ownership or remaining shop stock.
All Shops.example: Buying a bronze hatchet from Bob’s Brilliant Axes can become a shop-collection goal.

Quest Skill Reqs.what: This saved switch currently has no independent effect. Quest skill requirements continue to be checked by the ordinary task engine.
Quest Skill Reqs.example: No task is added here: Dragon Slayer remains a quest-completion goal governed by its ordinary access and requirement checks.

Boosting.what: Lets supported obtainable skill boosts help meet task requirements and affect which skill goal is shown. The picker handles fixed and percentage boosts, but cannot calculate every boost formula.
Boosting.example: With reachable Herblore 4 and an obtainable Greenman's ale, cleaning tarromin at level 5 can become available.

Token.what: Lets methods with small incidental XP gains count as repeatable training for required goals. This can raise how far the picker thinks you can train that skill.
Token.example: Mixing unfinished tarromin potions can count as a Herblore training route when the herbs and vials of water are obtainable.
Token.grindWarning: A tiny repeatable XP gain can imply training far beyond the level at which you unlock it.

Master skillcape.what: Allows the listed level-120 master cape goals when their seller and other requirements are reachable. These are separate from ordinary level-99 cape goals.
Master skillcape.example: Buying the Agility master cape becomes an eligible goal at virtual Agility 120 with access to its seller.
Master skillcape.grindWarning: Virtual level 120 in Agility requires 104,273,167 XP.

Cleaning Herbs.what: Controls active Herblore goals for cleaning herbs and mixing unfinished potions above level 1. Hidden recipes and their products still help the picker work out what else you can do.
Cleaning Herbs.example: Turning this off hides the clean-tarromin goal while the engine can still use its clean herb output.

Cleaning Herbs Primary.what: Lets listed herb-cleaning methods establish a required Herblore training route. The separate Cleaning Herbs switch controls whether those goals appear.
Cleaning Herbs Primary.example: Cleaning obtainable grimy tarromin can establish repeatable Herblore training when this is enabled.

Vinesweeper.what: Allows the listed Farming training method at Vinesweeper when you can reach the activity. Its Hunter method has a separate rule.
Vinesweeper.example: Playing Vinesweeper can become an available Farming method after its location is accessible.

Ogleroot.what: Allows the listed Hunter training method that feeds rabbits in Vinesweeper. Access to the activity still has to be established.
Ogleroot.example: Feeding an ogleroot to a Vinesweeper rabbit can become a Hunter training task.

Gnomeball.what: Allows the listed Gnome Ball methods to establish Agility and Ranged training when its field is reachable.
Gnomeball.example: Playing Gnome Ball can become a Ranged training method in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

Daemonheim training.what: Allows the listed training routes inside Daemonheim. This can make further skill requirements reachable while keeping dungeon equipment separate from surface supplies.
Daemonheim training.example: Training Attack inside Daemonheim becomes an eligible method when its dungeons are accessible.

Daemonheim tasks.what: Allows listed skill goals involving activities or equipment inside Daemonheim. The separate training rule controls whether its methods establish repeatable training.
Daemonheim tasks.example: Wielding an argonite weapon inside Daemonheim can become an Attack goal at level 60.

PortSkills.what: Requires all twelve port skills to be within reach of level 90 before any of their adventurer goals become chunk tasks.
PortSkills.example: If eleven port skills can reach 90 and the last cannot, none of these goals is required yet.
PortSkills.grindWarning: Once all twelve are within reach, each skill has its own level-90 goal.

Titles.what: Allows listed title-unlock goals when their recorded requirements are reachable. Other rules can still exclude titles tied to particular activities.
Titles.example: Earning Archmage can become a goal with Rune Memories and level 99 in both Magic and Runecrafting within reach.
Titles.grindWarning: Some titles require high levels or repeated activity completions.

DnD.what: Allows listed Distraction and Diversion tasks and the training or rewards they provide. Their location, timing and other rules still apply.
DnD.example: Building a God Statue can become an available Construction method when Copernicus Glyph is reachable.

DnD Flash Events.what: Allows the listed flash-event access and reward tasks, subject to their other rules. It does not predict when an event will spawn.
DnD Flash Events.example: Obtaining normal Demon Flash Mob rewards can become available when the listed location and group-content requirements are met.

Not Daily DnD.what: This saved option has no implemented task or timing filter here. Changing it does not remove daily activities or add weekly and monthly ones.
Not Daily DnD.example: No task is added here; building a monthly God Statue remains controlled by its existing activity and timing rules.

Uncharted.what: Allows listed gathering methods on Uncharted Isles when their resources and requirements are reachable. These methods can establish training or supply later recipes.
Uncharted.example: Catching an ornate tortle can become a Hunter goal at level 96 when the tortle and trap are obtainable.

Arc Log.what: Allows listed Arc journal collection goals. Their birds, resources or other entries still need an allowed source.
Arc Log.example: Spotting the Cyclosis Cockatiel can become an Arc journal goal when that bird is obtainable in the engine.

Menaphos Log.what: Allows listed Menaphos journal entries as collection goals. It does not complete the journal automatically.
Menaphos Log.example: Finding a Menaphite honey bee in amber can become a journal goal when the journal and amber entry are obtainable.

Costume Room.what: This old option does not generate storage goals here. Current house storage goals use House storage tasks instead.
Costume Room.example: No task is added by this saved name; storing the Mask of Dragith Nurn in an armour case is handled by House storage tasks.

Achievement.what: Shows eligible achievement goals in the active task list. Hidden achievements can still help the picker work out which requirements you meet and which rewards you can obtain.
Achievement.example: Turning this off removes Agility 5 from the active list without erasing its underlying achievement task.

Multiple Pickpockets.what: This saved option has no implemented task rule here. It does not change the listed multi-loot pickpocket goals.
Multiple Pickpockets.example: No task is added here; a farmer multi-loot pickpocket goal still follows the existing Thieving and Agility rules.

Multiple Agility.what: Allows listed Agility goals for the multi-loot bonuses used while pickpocketing. The target and the accompanying Thieving requirement still have to be available.
Multiple Agility.example: Pickpocketing a farmer for quadruple loot can become an Agility goal when its Agility and Thieving requirements are reachable.

F2P.what: Applies free-to-play restrictions to both players, including members-only tasks, equipment, training and travel. Turn it off to allow supported members content.
F2P.example: Turning this on removes the members-only Agility master cape goal, even if its seller and level requirement would otherwise be reachable.

Hard Mode Bosses.what: Allows listed tasks marked for harder boss modes. Boss drops and kill-count goals still follow their separate rules.
Hard Mode Bosses.example: Defeating Amascut, the Devourer at 500% or higher enrage in under ten minutes can become an Elite speed-kill goal when the other achievement rules allow it.

sources.title: Amascut, the Devourer (EM) Elite Speed Killer

Group Content.what: Allows listed activities and goals that need group participation. Their other requirements still apply, and the picker does not assemble a team.
Group Content.example: Participating in a sinkhole can become a Dungeoneering method when Sinkholes and its other activity rules allow it.

PVP.what: Allows the listed tasks tagged PVP, rather than enabling every form of player combat. Other differently named PvP options are separate saved names.
PVP.example: Casting Teleport Block can become a Magic goal when the spell requirements, runes and listed PvP location are reachable.

Hero Items.what: Allows listed hero-item goals that would otherwise be excluded by this rule. It does not make their rare sources more likely.
Hero Items.example: Obtaining Guildmaster Tony's mattock can become a skilling equipment goal when its item source and Archaeology requirement are reachable.
Hero Items.grindWarning: A hero-item goal can require an exceptionally rare reward.

Brawling Gloves.what: Allows listed brawling-glove goals within skilling equipment. The gloves must still have an obtainable source.
Brawling Gloves.example: Obtaining Agility brawling gloves can become a skilling equipment goal when their source is available.
Brawling Gloves.grindWarning: These gloves have limited charges, so obtaining them does not create a permanent XP bonus.

Unlock Abilities.what: Allows listed goals to unlock abilities through codices, items or activity rewards. It does not itself grant an ability or confirm that you have learned it.
Unlock Abilities.example: Unlocking Ingenuity of the Humans can become a goal when its ability codex is obtainable.

Sigil Abilities.what: Allows the listed former-sigil ability unlock goals alongside Unlock Abilities. Each unlock permanently adds an ability, while its item and skill requirements still apply.
Sigil Abilities.example: Unlocking Golden Touch can become a goal when its codex is obtainable and Magic 55 is reachable.
Sigil Abilities.grindWarning: Golden Touch needs 2,000 vital sparks. Collecting them through rare pickpocket rewards can take a long time.

Unlock Prayers.what: Allows listed prayer-unlock goals when their quest, item and level requirements are reachable. This does not change which prayers you have personally unlocked.
Unlock Prayers.example: Unlocking the Knight Waves training ground prayers can become a goal after King's Ransom is within reach.

PvM Relics.what: This rule has no matching combat-relic tasks in the current catalogue. It does not select a relic setup or allocate monolith energy.
PvM Relics.example: No task is added here; unlocking a combat relic at the mysterious monolith would need a supported goal before this switch could govern it.

KeyItem Bosses.what: This saved option currently has no effect. Entry-key rarity is not included in boss drop cutoffs or time estimates.
KeyItem Bosses.example: Turning this on leaves task lists and drop cutoffs unchanged; how an entry key should count still needs a rule decision.

Shooting Stars.what: Allows the listed crashed-star Mining methods, together with their Distraction and Diversion rule. It does not locate the next star for you.
Shooting Stars.example: Mining a size-1 crashed star can become an available Mining method at level 10.

Combat Mastery achievements.what: Allows listed Combat Mastery goals. Some miscellaneous combat achievements are also marked for this rule, so switching it off excludes those goals too.
Combat Mastery achievements.example: Giant Mole Novice Speed Killer can become an eligible achievement when the mole is reachable and the speed-kill switch is enabled.
Combat Mastery achievements.grindWarning: Combat tasks may require repeated boss kills, special restrictions or precise execution.

Speed Killer Achievements.what: Allows the listed timed boss-kill achievements within Combat Mastery. It does not estimate whether your current equipment can meet their timers.
Speed Killer Achievements.example: Defeating the Giant Mole solo in under five minutes can become a Combat Mastery goal.

Combat Master+.what: Allows listed Master and higher Combat Mastery goals when their other requirements are reachable. Lower-tier goals remain under their own rules.
Combat Master+.example: Barrows: Rise of the Six Master Speed Killer can become a goal when the boss and the other combat and speed-kill rules are available.

sources.title: Barrows: Rise of the Six Master Speed Killer

Combat Master+.grindWarning: These goals can require demanding boss conditions beyond merely reaching the fight.

Misc Combat Achievements.what: This older capitalised name does not control any supported tasks. Use Misc Combat achievements, with a lower-case achievements, for the listed combat goals.
Misc Combat Achievements.example: No task is added by this spelling; Mole Removal VI still follows Misc Combat achievements and its other rules.

Menaphos Events.what: Allows listed Menaphos event training methods. Access to Menaphos and the particular event still has to be available.
Menaphos Events.example: Siphoning a Menaphos soul obelisk for Prayer XP can become a method at Prayer 50.

Hunter Marks Slayer.what: This saved option has no implemented link between Hunter-mark rewards and Slayer training here.
Hunter Marks Slayer.example: No task is added here; earning Hunter marks on Anachronia remains governed by supported Hunter activities.

Material Blueprints.what: Allows listed Invention goals for discovering material blueprints at an inventor's workbench. Owning a material and knowing its blueprint remain different requirements.
Material Blueprints.example: Discovering refined components can become an Invention goal at level 22 with a reachable inventor's workbench.

Wandering implings.what: Allows the listed roaming impling-catching methods. These tasks do not require a listed fixed spawn, so a roaming catch can appear without locating an impling first.
Wandering implings.example: Catching a wandering baby impling can become a Hunter goal at level 17.

Comp achievements.what: Allows listed completionist achievement goals. A goal still needs its own skills, locations and prerequisites, and other family switches can further restrict it.
Comp achievements.example: Upgrading every Fort Forinthry building to tier 3 can become the A Fort Of My Own goal.
Comp achievements.grindWarning: Completionist goals can combine many separate upgrades and activities.

Trim achievements.what: Allows listed trimmed-completionist goals together with Comp achievements. It does not replace the ordinary completionist requirements.
Trim achievements.example: Buying every upgrade from Sydekix's Shop can become the A Druid's Sidekick goal.
Trim achievements.grindWarning: Trimmed requirements can demand long collections, repeated activities or high skill levels.

MQC achievements.what: Allows listed Master Quest Cape achievement goals. Their individual lore, quest and access requirements still apply.
MQC achievements.example: Finding and reading the scruffy note in the Scabarite Cavern can become the A bug in the system goal.

Misc achievements.what: Allows listed skill, exploration and activity achievements outside the other named families. Additional rules can still exclude a particular goal.
Misc achievements.example: Reaching Agility 5 can become an achievement goal when Level Up Achievements is also enabled.

Speedrunning.what: Allows listed timed activity achievements outside the boss speed-kill switch. The activity and any other family rules still have to be available.
Speedrunning.example: Completing a qualifying solo large frozen dungeon in under 6:15 can become Easy Freezy III.

Level Up Achievements.what: Allows listed skill-level achievement goals within Misc achievements. It can add an achievement obligation alongside the skill's normal highest-level task.
Level Up Achievements.example: Agility 5 can become a separate achievement goal when its level is reachable.

No RuneScore.what: Allows the listed achievements marked as awarding no RuneScore. It does not automatically find every achievement with a score of zero.
No RuneScore.example: Reaching virtual Agility 120 can become an achievement goal when the miscellaneous and level-up rules also allow it.
No RuneScore.grindWarning: Virtual level-120 achievements can require substantially more XP than level 99.

Slayer Contracts.what: Allows listed contract methods as Slayer training routes. The issuer, applicable targets and other requirements still need to be reachable.
Slayer Contracts.example: Completing a Slayer contract from Markus can become an available Slayer training method.

Hide Partial Products.what: Removes listed unfinished-product skill goals above level 1 from the active view. Their recipes and products remain available to the engine.
Hide Partial Products.example: Turning this on hides a listed unfinished-potion skill goal while its ingredients can still be processed for later recipes.

Timegated.what: Requires listed tasks that take repeated visits over weeks, including farm upgrades and port voyages. With this off, these are not chunk tasks; a single short growth cycle does not count.
Timegated.example: Constructing a monthly God Statue can become a Construction method when its Distraction and Diversion rule and location also allow it.
Timegated.grindWarning: Enabling this can require waiting for an activity reset or limited availability.

Cosmetics.what: Allows listed cosmetic collection goals inside their parent collections. It does not treat every appearance item as independently obtainable.
Cosmetics.example: Obtaining Glacor's Adornment can become a boss collection goal when the Arch-Glacor reward source and collection rules allow it.

Secondary Bird Nests.what: Allows the listed nest-looting tasks to produce their declared loot. It governs this supply route rather than every source of nests or every Woodcutting goal.
Secondary Bird Nests.example: Looting an obtainable seed bird's nest can add the listed seed-loot supply route.

House storage tasks.what: Adds supported house storage and display goals when the items, current furniture recipe and housing requirements are reachable. Automatic book retrieval does not generate a fill goal.
House storage tasks.example: Storing the Mask of Dragith Nurn in an armour case can become a goal when the mask and a compatible case are obtainable.

Rare Drop Inclusive.what: Includes sources exactly equal to your rare-drop cutoff when that cutoff is active. It does not change the rate or remove the other source requirements.
Rare Drop Inclusive.example: With Rare Drop off and a 1/1 cutoff, the King Black Dragon's always-dropped bones can supply a bury-dragon-bones task when equality is allowed.

Secondary Primary Inclusive.what: Includes item sources exactly equal to the required-training rate cutoff. It affects training and consumable-equipment checks of item sources without changing drop odds.
Secondary Primary Inclusive.example: At a 1/1 training-source cutoff, an always-dropped dragon-bone source can qualify for the bury-dragon-bones training route.

Every Drop BGH.what: Includes obtainable Big Game Hunter outputs in Every Drop collection goals. The parent Every Drop rule and the hunting method's requirements still apply.
Every Drop BGH.example: Collecting dinosaur bones from a reachable Bagrada rex hunt can become an Every Drop goal.
Every Drop BGH.grindWarning: Collecting a particular hunting reward may take repeated hunts.

Every Drop Thieving.what: Includes supported Thieving outputs in Every Drop collection goals, except outputs marked hidden. The parent rule and source access still apply.
Every Drop Thieving.example: Collecting a potato seed from an obtainable farmer pickpocket can become an Every Drop goal.

Fill Costume Room.what: This old saved name does not generate storage goals here. House storage tasks is the supported switch for current furniture.
Fill Costume Room.example: No task is added by this saved name; storing the Mask of Dragith Nurn uses House storage tasks instead.

Abilities.what: Allows the small set of listed skill goals for using abilities. It is distinct from Unlock Abilities, which governs the separate unlock collection goals.
Abilities.example: Using Meteor Strike can become an Attack goal at level 90 when its recorded requirements are reachable.

Misc Combat achievements.what: Allows listed miscellaneous combat achievements, including boss kill milestones. Some also require Combat Mastery achievements because both rules apply.
Misc Combat achievements.example: Defeating the Giant Mole 100 times can become the Mole Removal VI goal when both this switch and Combat Mastery achievements allow it.

XP Lamps.what: Allows the listed experience-lamp usage goals. This rule alone does not turn every lamp reward into a repeatable training method.
XP Lamps.example: Using an experience lamp from the Ports Reward Shop on Agility can become a listed goal when its lamp source is obtainable.

Show Best in Slot Weight Tasks.what: Adds per-slot equipment goals using verified worn weights, choosing the lighter eligible item. Items without usable weight data and combined weapon loadouts are outside this comparison.
Show Best in Slot Weight Tasks.example: Boots of lightness can become the weight-reducing feet goal when obtainable, wearable and lightest among the supported choices.

Collection Log Bosses.what: This saved collection name has no implemented task rule here. Supported collection families use their own rule names.
Collection Log Bosses.example: No task is added by this saved name; a boss drop such as Glacor's Adornment still needs the appropriate supported collection rule and source.

Collection Log Raids.what: This saved collection name has no implemented task rule here. Supported collection families use their own rule names.
Collection Log Raids.example: No task is added by this saved name; a Mazcab ability codex raid reward still needs the appropriate supported collection rule and source.

Collection Log Clues.what: This saved collection name has no implemented task rule here. Supported collection families use their own rule names.
Collection Log Clues.example: No task is added by this saved name; obtaining a robin hood hat from a clue reward still needs a supported collection goal and source.

Collection Log Minigames.what: This saved collection name has no implemented task rule here. Supported collection families use their own rule names.
Collection Log Minigames.example: No task is added by this saved name; obtaining a fighter torso still needs the supported Barbarian Assault source and collection rules.

Collection Log Other.what: This saved collection name has no implemented task rule here. Supported collection families use their own rule names.
Collection Log Other.example: No task is added by this saved name; spotting the Cyclosis Cockatiel still needs its supported Arc journal goal and access.

Stuffables.what: This saved option has no implemented stuffed-trophy generator here. It cannot add taxidermy or house-display goals by itself.
Stuffables.example: No task is added here; obtaining a stuffed crawling hand would need a supported goal and its own item source.

Money Unlockables.what: Allows the listed coin-funded unlock goals, together with any other rules on each task. It does not calculate how long earning their coins will take.
Money Unlockables.example: Obtaining the Billionaire title can become a goal when Titles and the listed Deep Sea Fishing location also allow it.
Money Unlockables.grindWarning: The Billionaire title requires donating a total of 5 billion coins to the Deep Sea Whirlpool.

Fill POH.what: This saved option has no implemented fill-the-house generator here. Current storage and display goals use House storage tasks.
Fill POH.example: No task is added here; storing the Mask of Dragith Nurn still needs the supported house-storage rule and furniture.

Primary Spawn.what: This older singular name has no implemented source effect here. Primary Spawns, with a final s, controls whether spawns count toward required training.
Primary Spawn.example: No task is added by this old name; making super defence potions with spawned white berries still follows Primary Spawns and the usual Herblore rules.

tasks.cache-skill-guide.what: Enables the reviewed skill-guide additions. The current additions are four Cooking no-burn milestones, so the separate milestone switch must also be on to create goals.
tasks.cache-skill-guide.example: With both guide switches enabled and shrimps and a cooking facility reachable, the Cooking 34 no-burn-shrimps milestone can be added.

tasks.skill-guide-milestones.what: Allows informational level thresholds from the skill-guide overlay to become personal goals. The main skill-guide switch must also be enabled.
tasks.skill-guide-milestones.example: The standard no-burn-shrimps threshold at Cooking 34 can become a goal rather than remaining information only.

tasks.cache-combat-corrections.what: Applies reviewed level corrections to listed combat tasks. It changes their numeric level requirements without supplying the needed codex, quest completion or equipment.
tasks.cache-combat-corrections.example: The Greater Sonic Wave usage task can be available at Magic 6 instead of the retained level 75 when its other requirements are met.

access.shared.what: Lets your partner’s territory contribute task access and supplies through supported connections. Your required goals and next rolls still follow your own map.
access.shared.example: A partner's reachable source of raw shrimps can help make your own cook-shrimps task possible when shared access connects that source.

travel.automatic.what: Checks travel using your recorded quest completions and skill levels imported by Sync levels. Missing levels can be estimated from training you can reach; runes, fares and route access still matter.
travel.automatic.example: A synced Magic level meeting Varrock Teleport, with its runes and required spellbook available, can add that destination without manually entering the level again.

access.transport.what: Uses verified personal transport routes to extend reachable sections and offer their destinations as roll candidates. Route requirements, fares and landing evidence still apply.
access.transport.example: No task is added directly; a verified route into a new area can make its existing cook-shrimps task reachable after that area is unlocked.

roll.selected.what: Includes your manually selected chunks in the next roll pool, subject to the remaining exclusions. This changes candidate selection rather than task rules.
roll.selected.example: No task is added directly; selecting a chunk containing a shrimp-cooking facility makes it a roll candidate, not an immediate cook-shrimps obligation.

roll.adjacent.what: Includes adjacent chunks from your own unlocked map when the neighbour mode allows automatic candidates. Reachable mode requires a verified walking connection.
roll.adjacent.example: No task is added directly; a neighbouring shrimp-cooking location can enter the roll pool before its cook-shrimps task becomes an obligation.

roll.neighborMode.what: Chooses manual candidates, neighbouring chunk borders, or verified accessible walking connections. The adjacent-candidate switch must also allow automatic neighbours.
roll.neighborMode.example: No task is added directly; accessible mode can exclude a neighbouring cooking location with no verified walking route, leaving cook-shrimps unavailable there.

roll.clearSelected.what: Clears your manually selected candidate list after an unlock when enabled. It does not remove unlocked chunks or completed tasks.
roll.clearSelected.example: No task is added or removed; unlocking a selected shrimp-cooking chunk clears remaining selections while its cook-shrimps task follows normal access.

roll.walkable.what: Filters out nearby roll candidates marked as having no walkable ground. Manually selected destinations and verified travel arrivals bypass this check; Accessible mode checks walking connections itself.
roll.walkable.example: No task is added directly; excluding a non-walkable cooking location keeps its cook-shrimps task from becoming a new obligation through that roll.

roll.teleports.what: Includes destinations of available declared teleports and supported automatically derived global routes. Consumable and owner-scope settings still apply.
roll.teleports.example: No task is added directly; an available Lumbridge Teleport can add its destination to the roll pool before any local cook-shrimps goal becomes yours.

roll.teleportScope.what: Chooses whether teleport candidates come from your own travel records or every group member's. It does not transfer another member's personal unlock evidence to you.
roll.teleportScope.example: No task is added directly; group scope can offer a partner's declared Lumbridge Teleport destination while local cook-shrimps obligations still follow your map.

roll.consumableTeleports.what: Allows consumable teleport routes to supply roll candidates when their other requirements are met. Non-consumable destinations remain eligible through their own routes.
roll.consumableTeleports.example: No task is added directly; allowing the rune-consuming Varrock Teleport can offer its destination before an existing local task becomes your obligation.

tasks.completion.what: Sets whether a group challenge is satisfied by any member, every member, or only the current member. It preserves each member's separate personal game-completion evidence.
tasks.completion.example: If one member completes Imp Catcher, any-member mode can satisfy that challenge for the group; all-member mode keeps it required for the others.

Additional Money Unlockables.what: This saved option has no implemented unlock generator here. Supported coin-funded goals use Money Unlockables and each goal's other rules.
Additional Money Unlockables.example: No task is added here; earning the Billionaire title still follows Money Unlockables and its supported source requirements.

Boss Level.what: This saved option does not set a boss level or change combat requirements here. Supported boss tasks retain their recorded access and skill checks.
Boss Level.example: No task is added here; a King Black Dragon goal still depends on the supported boss rules and reachable fight.

Cleaning herbs.what: This older spelling has no effect here. Cleaning Herbs controls active cleaning goals, and Cleaning Herbs Primary controls their training role.
Cleaning herbs.example: No task is added by this spelling; cleaning tarromin still follows the correctly capitalised cleaning and training switches.

DnD Skilling.what: This saved name has no independent activity rule here. Supported skilling diversions follow the Distraction and Diversion switch and their other activity rules.
DnD Skilling.example: No task is added here; building a God Statue still follows Distraction and Diversion and Timegated.

Forestry.what: This saved name has no supported RS3 task group or engine behavior here. Changing it does not add Woodcutting methods.
Forestry.example: No task is added here; cutting an oak remains governed by the existing Woodcutting task and access rules.

Full Healing.what: This saved option has no implemented healing-task or food-source effect here. It does not change the requirements of supported food tasks.
Full Healing.example: No task is added here; cooking a shark still follows its existing Cooking level, ingredient and facility checks.

Jars.what: This saved option has no supported jar-collection generator or verified link to tasks here. It does not alter existing Hunter catches.
Jars.example: No task is added here; catching a baby impling still follows its supported Hunter and source requirements.

Kili Knowledge.what: This saved option has no implemented Kili-task rule here. Supported Necromancy and quest tasks retain their own requirements.
Kili Knowledge.example: No task is added here; completing Kili Row still follows its existing quest and Necromancy requirements.

Partial Products.what: This saved option has no supported product filter here. Hide Partial Products is the implemented switch for suppressing marked unfinished-product goals.
Partial Products.example: No task is added or hidden here; an unfinished-potion goal still follows Hide Partial Products and the usual Herblore checks.

PvP Minigame.what: This saved option has no implemented PvP-minigame rule here. Supported activities follow their own activity rules and ordinary access checks.
PvP Minigame.example: No task is added here; a Gnome Ball training task still follows its existing activity rule, independent of this saved option.

Superheat Furnace.what: This saved option has no implemented furnace, spell or prayer effect here. It cannot create an extra training route by itself.
Superheat Furnace.example: No task is added here; using Superheat Form would still require a supported task and that prayer's own unlock and level requirements.
